RECOMMENDATION: DON'T RAISE IT
LIKELIHOOD: 25

A panel's gender composition alone is not evidence of bias. Selection committees are typically formed based on departmental roles, subfield relevance, or administrative availability. Furthermore, lecturer appointments frequently prioritize specific curricular needs, teaching approach, and relevant industry experience over publication counts alone.

Raising accusations of gender bias based purely on committee demographics is legally unsubstantiated and could severely harm your academic reputation. Instead, send a polite follow-up requesting constructive feedback on your interview performance. Seek to understand how the department weighed industry background against research output, and consult a faculty ombudsman confidentially only if formal university rules regarding committee composition were breached.
